geography: World Bank countries and economies with a non-aggregate region and at least one published value in the series. Codes follow the World Bank registry, including XKX for Kosovo.
transformations: Rows are grouped under their source economy codes. All years within the observed series span appear. Null in JSON and blank in CSV represent an unavailable observation. Numeric values retain the precision returned by the publisher. Explicit zeros and status codes are retained.
validation: Each observation from the API for every non-aggregate economy, including unavailable years, was checked for equality with its entry in the separately downloaded official wide CSV release.

resource-depletion-energy.name: Adjusted savings: energy depletion (% of GNI)
resource-depletion-energy.definition: Energy depletion is the ratio of the value of the stock of energy resources to the remaining reserve lifetime (capped at 25 years). It covers coal, crude oil, and natural gas. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of Gross National Income (GNI) which is the total income earned by all residents within an economic territory during an accounting period. It is equal to gross domestic product plus earned income receivable from abroad minus earned income payable abroad.
resource-depletion-energy.sourceOrganizations:
Staff estimates, World Bank (WB);
The Changing Wealth of Nations: Measuring Sustainable Development in the New Millennium, World Bank (WB)

resource-depletion-forest.name: Adjusted savings: net forest depletion (% of GNI)
resource-depletion-forest.definition: Net forest depletion is calculated as the product of unit resource rents and the excess of roundwood harvest over natural growth. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of Gross National Income (GNI) which is the total income earned by all residents within an economic territory during an accounting period. It is equal to gross domestic product plus earned income receivable from abroad minus earned income payable abroad.
resource-depletion-forest.sourceOrganizations:
Staff estimates, World Bank (WB);
The Changing Wealth of Nations: Measuring Sustainable Development in the New Millennium, World Bank (WB)

resource-depletion-mineral.name: Adjusted savings: mineral depletion (% of GNI)
resource-depletion-mineral.definition: Mineral depletion is the ratio of the value of the stock of mineral resources to the remaining reserve lifetime (capped at 25 years). It covers tin, gold, lead, zinc, iron, copper, nickel, silver, bauxite, and phosphate. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of Gross National Income (GNI) which is the total income earned by all residents within an economic territory during an accounting period. It is equal to gross domestic product plus earned income receivable from abroad minus earned income payable abroad.
resource-depletion-mineral.sourceOrganizations:
Staff estimates, World Bank (WB);
The Changing Wealth of Nations: Measuring Sustainable Development in the New Millennium, World Bank (WB)

resource-depletion-total.name: Adjusted savings: natural resources depletion (% of GNI)
resource-depletion-total.definition: Natural resource depletion is the sum of net forest depletion, energy depletion, and mineral depletion. Net forest depletion is unit resource rents times the excess of roundwood harvest over natural growth. Energy depletion is the ratio of the value of the stock of energy resources to the remaining reserve lifetime (capped at 25 years). It covers coal, crude oil, and natural gas. Mineral depletion is the ratio of the value of the stock of mineral resources to the remaining reserve lifetime (capped at 25 years). It covers tin, gold, lead, zinc, iron, copper, nickel, silver, bauxite, and phosphate. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of Gross National Income (GNI) which is the total income earned by all residents within an economic territory during an accounting period. It is equal to gross domestic product plus earned income receivable from abroad minus earned income payable abroad.
resource-depletion-total.sourceOrganizations:
Staff estimates, World Bank (WB);
The Changing Wealth of Nations: Measuring Sustainable Development in the New Millennium, World Bank (WB)

methodology.source: World Bank, The Changing Wealth of Nations, distributed in World Development Indicators.
methodology.interpretation: The total and component series are retained independently. A missing component or total stays blank. Each series represents an annual monetary estimate. The rent denominator is GDP and the depletion denominator is gross national income (GNI).
methodology.measure: Energy and mineral depletion use the value of the resource stock divided by remaining reserve life, capped at 25 years. Net forest depletion values timber harvest in excess of natural growth. A zero forest-depletion estimate can coexist with a loss of forest area.
